lots.what_it_is: Photographic (sublimation) mug-making kit in a black tub plus a carton, title PHOTOGRAPHIC MUG KIT. (1) A Cricut Mug Press: white body, mint green cradle, cricut logo on the front, lid open, mains lead stored in the cradle; model label not visible, but dealer listings for this press all give model CMP01200. (2) An unbranded lever-type mug heat press: black frame with T-handle and pressure knob, plus a separate digital controller box (TEMP and TIME displays, TEMP/SET/TIME lights, minus, MODE, plus and start buttons, red rocker switch, aviation-type plug); the common generic single-mug press style, heating pad not clearly seen. (3) A carton of about ten boxed 11oz two-tone sublimation blank mugs (boxes hand-labelled white black, white pink and pink glitter; one mug out with a pink inner and handle), possibly more underneath. Also in the tub: a large dark grey flat sheet, two white and three or four black mug-sized boxes (contents unknown). The title does not mention Cricut.

lots.guide_summary: All same-item and close evidence is ASKING; there is no SOLD or UNSOLD result for any item in the lot. Cricut Mug Press: used dealer asks $107.65 to $175 (six Cash Converters listings, most with a 30 or 90 day warranty, two already marked down) and new $299 (Cricut AU and Spotlight, both pages opened). Generic lever mug press: used dealer asks $84.15 and $89 (close), with a branded Permasub at $169.95, a Vevor roller press at $99 and a new Vevor tumbler press at A$151.90 as category guides. Blank two-tone 11oz mugs: $4.50 each new, so about $45 for the ten or so in the carton. The range shown ($84.15 to $299) covers the press entries; the mug price is per unit. Adding the cheapest used asks for both presses and ten new mugs gives about $237, a retail asking total, not a value. Context only: three Gowans craft cutters sold for $52 to $115 hammer (Feb to Sep 2026), the level local buyers pay for second-hand hobby craft machines. All prices AUD, no currency conversion.
lots.working: keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0: no SOLD price within 24 months was found for a Cricut Mug Press, a generic mug press or blank mugs (Gowans API re-checked for cricut, mug press, heat press, sublimation, mug kit and photographic: no such lot; Armitage's last six sales, 17 Jun to 30 Sep 2026, held no Cricut, mug press or heat press lot; WebSearch was not available this run). The three Gowans SOLD entries are craft cutters and cannot set a bid. For context only, not a bid: if the Cricut press resold privately for about $100 (below the lowest dealer ask), less about 13% eBay fees and $20 postage, it would support (100 x 0.87 - 20) / 2.44 = $27 hammer for the Cricut alone. Buyer's premium 22% incl. GST (all-in = hammer x 1.22); pickup only from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay, inbound freight $0.

lots.question_for_armitage: Does the Cricut Mug Press power on and heat, and has it been used before (new units need a one-off activation through Cricut's app)? lots.what_it_is: A clear tub of played-with, mostly built modern LEGO with loose bricks and booklets (title VARIOUS LEGO), no boxes and no minifigures seen. Identified against Brickset images: Harry Potter 76421 Dobby the House-Elf (403 pcs, 2023), built on its black display base, with its white and lavender birthday-cake accessory loose in the card tray; Harry Potter 76433 Mandrake (579 pcs, 2024), built in its terracotta pot; and very likely 76434 Aragog in the Forbidden Forest (195 pcs, 2024), the brick-built spider only (Harry and Ron minifigures and web scene not seen). All three retired 31 Dec 2025 (Brickset; RRP US$34.99, US$69.99 and US$19.99). Loose Speed Champions booklets for 76921 Audi S1 e-tron quattro, 76914 Ferrari 812 Competizione and a Lotus Evija (76907 by its cover; number partly hidden), with no built cars seen. Not identified: a pastel chequerboard build with a piano keyboard and blossoms (Friends or similar), white and blue train panels, loose orange flowers and lime stems (Botanicals style), a blue and teal creature with orange nozzles, white and grey builds, a house booklet, a text-heavy booklet with large WI letters (possibly the Wizarding World intro pages of one of the Harry Potter booklets, unconfirmed) and a card tray of loose bricks with a $39.99 store ticket. Completeness of every model is unknown.
lots.score_reason: Recognisable retired Harry Potter display builds (Dobby, Mandrake, very likely Aragog) plus booklets and mixed parts. The identified pieces are worth about A$75 to A$90 on US sold prices and Tasmanian tubs of built LEGO make $55 to $130 hammer, so a real value of roughly $80 to $150: 5, held down by unknown completeness.

lots.guide_summary: Mostly SOLD. Close whole-lot comparables (tubs or boxes of built modern LEGO) sold for $55 to $130 hammer in Tasmania between Feb and Oct 2026: Armitage $80 and $105 (8 Jul 2026), Gowans $55 to $130 (7 lots). Same-item component sales (US eBay via PriceCharting, built or loose, no box): Dobby A$7.19 to A$28.74 (typical A$14), Mandrake A$24.66 to A$50.28 (typical A$29), Aragog A$4.67 to A$10.42, and the three orphan Speed Champions booklets A$10.06 to A$14.37 each; the identified parts add up to about A$75 at the lowest and A$91 at typical prices, before fees and postage. Category guides (other Armitage and Gowans LEGO lots, two boxed sets, bulk tubs, train lots) ran $35 to $150 hammer. No UNSOLD result found. ASKING: only the Brickset model values (used about US$15 to 28 a set). The guide range ($55 to $130) is the close whole-lot evidence. Hammer prices exclude buyer's premium (Armitage 22%; Gowans premium extra). USD at 1.437 (ECB via frankfurter.dev, 16 Oct 2026).
lots.working: Keep, from same-item SOLD sales (built or loose, no box, last 24 months), lowest of each item, US$ at 1.437: Dobby 76421 US$5.00 = A$7.19, Mandrake 76433 US$17.16 = A$24.66 (the US$9.99 glued sale is dropped as not comparable), Aragog 76434 US$3.25 = A$4.67, booklets 76914 US$10.00 = A$14.37, 76921 US$7.00 = A$10.06 and 76907 US$9.99 = A$14.36. Total A$75.31 / 1.22 = $61.73, round down = $60. Cross-check: Tasmanian close tubs of built LEGO made $55 to $130 hammer (Armitage $80 and $105), so $60 sits at the low end of what these rooms pay; the train panels, flowers, Friends builds and loose bricks are not valued. Flip, parting out on eBay AU at typical sold prices: Dobby A$14.37 (US$10) + Mandrake A$28.74 (US$20) + Aragog A$8.62 (US$6) + booklets A$14.37 + A$10.06 + A$14.36 = A$90.52, less eBay fees of about 13% (A$11.77) and outbound postage of about A$49 (three parcels at A$10 to 15, three large letters at about A$4) = A$29.75 / 2.44 = $12.19, round down = $10. Buyer's premium 22% incl. GST (all-in = hammer x 1.22); pickup from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Dobby and Mandrake match Brickset images closely and the booklet numbers 76921 and 76914 are read, with many matching SOLD results opened (PriceCharting sold lists and Tasmanian hammer prices on past catalogue pages and the Gowans API). Held at Medium because completeness and condition are unknown, Aragog is very likely but not certain, the component sales are US eBay prices, and much of the tub is unidentified.

lots.question_for_armitage: Are there any minifigures in the tub (especially Harry and Ron from the Aragog set)? Are Dobby's diary accessory and the Mandrake's name tile there, and are the Dobby, Mandrake or Aragog instruction booklets included (the text booklet marked WI)? Roughly how full and heavy is the tub, and are there any non-LEGO bricks mixed in?

lots.what_it_is: Avon 1876 Cape Cod ruby red pressed glass (Avon's collectable range sold from 1975 to the mid 1990s), identified by the pattern (diamond-hatched heart band, starburst centres, scalloped rims, hexagonal feet) and the catalogue title (2 BOXES OF AVON GLASS - DINNER WARE, NAPKIN RINGS, ETC). About 60 to 80 pieces: a tall stack of dinner plates, further stacks of smaller plates, two stacks of rimmed soup or dessert bowls, a larger bowl, the big diamond-cut serving bowl, 4 footed (pedestal) mugs, 5 hexagonal-base salt or pepper shakers, about 13 napkin rings, a dinner plate displayed upright and a small hexagonal tray with gold script and a gold flower motif (unread). No AVON base marks are visible (bases not shown; some Cape Cod pieces are marked). Lot 470 in the same sale is a further 3 boxes of the same pattern (per the prep notes).
lots.score_reason: A large collection of a recognised collectable Avon pattern; US asks of about US$5 to 12 a piece suggest a real value above $80 for 60 to 80 pieces, but there is no sold price, Tasmanian ruby glass sells for $30 to $50 or passes in, and more of the same pattern (lot 470) is in this sale: 5.

lots.guide_summary: No same-item SOLD or UNSOLD result exists. The guide range (A$212.68 to A$359.25) is three Poshmark US asking prices for 20 to 26 piece Avon Cape Cod sets (one live and unsold after five weeks, two marked sold at the list price, one of those from 2024), each about a third the size of lot 468; component asks run about US$4 to US$17.50 a piece. Tasmanian evidence is much weaker: 6 SOLD category guides at $20 to $50 hammer (plain ruby or red glass lots, plus one small mixed Avon lot with two Cape Cod candlesticks at $20) and 3 UNSOLD passes of plain ruby goblets at Gowans in May 2026. Of the 21 surviving entries, 6 are sold (all category guides), 3 unsold and 12 asking. USD at 1.437 (ECB via frankfurter.dev, 16 Oct 2026).
lots.working: keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0: no SOLD price within 24 months for an Avon Cape Cod set or collection (Gowans API re-checked for avon and cape cod: only the two-candlestick mixed lot; Armitage's last six sales held no Cape Cod lot; WebSearch was not available this run). The ruby glass SOLD entries are different glass and cannot set a bid, and Poshmark list prices are asking prices. For context only: at about US$5 a piece, the low end of the US asks, 60 pieces would be about US$300 (A$431) at US retail before postage, but Tasmanian ruby glass lots make $30 to $50 hammer and often pass in. Buyer's premium 22% incl. GST (all-in = hammer x 1.22); pickup only from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay (heavy and fragile), inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: The pattern match is good and the title says Avon, but no base marks are seen, the condition of the stacked rims is unknown, and every Cape Cod price is a US asking price; there is no same-item sold result.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped: all 21 entries were opened and their price, date and kind match the researcher. Corrections: the Poshmark 26-piece set, 24-piece set and single dinner plate listings return HTTP 404 status to curl, but the listing data (price, status and dates) is embedded in the page and matched; the researcher's mentions of the same seller's other sold-out sets (27 Oct and 11 Sep 2025) and a 2022 30-piece set were not checked and are not used; the 4 dessert plates listing calls them coasters in its text, so that piece type is uncertain.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: the whole collection laid out; the pattern is consistent with Avon 1876 Cape Cod throughout (heart and diamond-hatch band, hexagonal feet on the mugs and shakers); I count 4 footed mugs, 5 shakers, 3 napkin rings in front plus about 10 in the serving bowl, and stacks of plates and bowls (roughly 50 to 60 flat pieces). Photo 2: close view of mugs, shakers and napkin rings, glass looks clean with no chips visible at this resolution; the small hexagonal tray's gold script stays unreadable when cropped and enlarged. Photo 3: flash-washed close-up of the napkin rings in the bowl, some dusty or smeared. Bases and marks not shown.
lots.condition: Appears clean and undamaged at photo resolution, but the rims of stacked plates and bowls cannot be seen properly, so chips are possible. Stacked loose in 2 boxes; heavy and fragile.
lots.question_for_armitage: Any chips or cracks on the plate and bowl rims, and how many of each piece are there (dinner plates, smaller plates, bowls)? Are any pieces marked AVON on the base? What does the gold script on the small hexagonal tray say?
